llm.summary: The skill's instructions mostly match a packing-and-booking helper but contain several operational and provenance inconsistencies (unknown CLI package, mandatory global npm install, and optional filesystem logging) that warrant caution before installing or running it.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (packing lists + booking support) is consistent with the runtime behavior: the skill forces use of a travel-focused CLI (flyai) to produce packing and booking outputs. However there are small mismatches: the description calls out Fliggy (Alibaba) while every runtime command targets an @fly-ai/flyai-cli package; no homepage/source is provided for the package or skill, and the skill claims booking capabilities but does not describe how credentials/authorization for bookings would be handled.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md requires the agent to (a) check for and — if missing — install a global npm package and (b) refuse to answer from its training data, sourcing every answer from CLI output only. It also mandates that every result include booking links from the CLI and prescribes output formatting. The runbook suggests writing an execution log to .flyai-execution-log.json if filesystem writes are available. These instructions reach outside pure 'answer generation' into package installation, network/CLI calls, and local file writes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec in the registry metadata; instead SKILL.md instructs running `npm i -g @fly-ai/flyai-cli`. Installing a global npm package from an unverified package name can execute arbitrary code (postinstall scripts, etc.). The package origin and trustworthiness are not documented (no homepage or registry verification), raising moderate risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request environment variables, credentials, or config paths — this is proportionate and reduces immediate exfiltration risk. That said, the skill claims booking features without requesting auth tokens or explaining how bookings/auth will be performed, which is an unexplained gap (it may rely on the flyai CLI to handle auth, but that is not documented here).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not force-enabled (always: false) and does not request elevated system privileges. However it instructs installing a global npm tool and (optionally) appending execution logs to a local .flyai-execution-log.json file, which introduces persistent filesystem artifacts and modifies system state. This is notable but not necessarily malicious.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill looks like a coherent packing-and-booking helper, but exercise caution before letting it run: 1) It instructs installing a global npm package (@fly-ai/flyai-cli) from an unknown source — global npm installs can run arbitrary code during install. Verify the npm package publisher and inspect the package (or run installation in a sandbox/VM) before allowing it. 2) The skill may write an execution log (.flyai-execution-log.json) to your workspace; if you don't want persistent logs, run it in a temporary directory or deny filesystem writes. 3) There is a provenance mismatch (mentions Fliggy but uses a 'flyai' CLI) and no homepage/source — ask the publisher for the package homepage, Git repo, and clarification on how bookings/auth are handled. 4) If you permit it to run, consider running the npm install manually yourself and reviewing its behavior (postinstall scripts, network calls) rather than letting an agent do it autonomously. If you are uncomfortable or cannot validate the CLI package, decline installation or run the skill in an isolated environment.
